ei.title: Distress and Eustress: Two Sides of Stress

fullPassage: When you are about to go on stage or perhaps take the microphone in a work presentation, do you feel sweaty, get flushed, have a dry mouth, or taste metal? Before taking an exam, does your breathing quicken? These are signs of your body activating your stress response or sympathetic nervous system. But stress is bad, right? Actually, stress isn't always bad. In fact, there are two types of stress: distress (what we normally think of as "stress") and eustress (beneficial stress that motivates us). Coming from the same root as the word euphoria ("eu" meaning good), eustress has been shown to induce different physiological changes to distress, including less strain on your cardiovascular system and a burst of the love hormone oxytocin, which helps heal damage to your heart. Meditation techniques can channel distress into eustress to help you approach whatever challenge or task you face with a clear, calm mind that is ready to focus.

questions.passage: When you are about to go on stage, do you feel sweaty, get flushed, have a dry mouth, or taste metal? Before taking an exam, does your breathing (A)[quicken / slow]? These are signs of your body (B)[activating / deactivating] your stress response or sympathetic nervous system. Actually, stress isn't (C)[always / never] bad. There are two types of stress.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① quicken — activating — always: 호흡이 '빨라지다', 스트레스 반응 '활성화', '항상' 나쁜 것은 아님.
❌ ② slow — activating — always: (A) 호흡이 '느려지는' 것이 아님.
❌ ③ quicken — deactivating — always: (B) 'deactivating(비활성화)'은 반대.
❌ ④ quicken — activating — never: (C) 'never'은 반대 의미.

questions.passage: But stress is bad, right? Actually, stress isn't always bad. In fact, there are two types of stress: distress (what we normally think of as "stress") and eustress ((A)[beneficial / harmful] stress that motivates us). Coming from the same root as the word euphoria ("eu" meaning (B)[good / bad]), eustress has been shown to induce different physiological changes to distress, including less strain on your cardiovascular system and a burst of the love hormone oxytocin, which helps (C)[heal / worsen] damage to your heart. This makes eustress valuable.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ beneficial — good — heal: '유익한' 스트레스, 'eu'는 '좋은', 심장 손상 '치유'.
❌ ① harmful — good — heal: (A) 반대.
❌ ② beneficial — bad — heal: (B) 'eu'는 '좋은'.
❌ ④ beneficial — good — worsen: (C) '악화'는 반대.

questions.passage: There are two types of stress: distress and eustress. Eustress is beneficial stress that motivates us. Eustress has been shown to induce different (A)[physiological / psychological] changes to distress, including less (B)[strain / relief] on your cardiovascular system and a burst of the love hormone oxytocin, which helps heal damage to your heart. Meditation techniques can (C)[channel / block] distress into eustress to help you approach challenges. This is a valuable mental skill.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② physiological — strain — channel: '생리적' 변화, 심혈관 '부담' 감소, 디스트레스를 유스트레스로 '돌림'.
❌ ① psychological — strain — channel: (A) '심리적'이 아닌 '생리적'.
❌ ③ physiological — relief — channel: (B) 'relief(안도)'는 반대.
❌ ④ physiological — strain — block: (C) 'block(막다)'은 반대.

questions.passage: When you are about to go on stage or perhaps take the microphone in a work presentation, do you feel ①<u>sweaty</u>, get flushed, have a dry mouth, or taste metal? These are signs of your body ②<u>activating</u> your stress response or sympathetic nervous system. Stress isn't always bad. In fact, there are two types of stress: distress and ③<u>eustress</u>. Meditation techniques can channel distress into eustress to help you approach challenges with a ④<u>confused</u>, calm mind.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ confused(혼란스러운) → clear(맑은). 원문은 'clear, calm mind(맑고 차분한 마음)'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① sweaty: 땀 흘리는. 적절.
❌ ② activating: 활성화하는. 적절.
❌ ③ eustress: 유스트레스. 적절.
✅ ④ confused → clear: 원문은 clear. confused는 반대.
det.tip: clear mind(맑은 마음) ↔ confused mind(혼란스러운 마음)

questions.passage: There are two types of stress: distress (what we normally think of as "stress") and eustress (①<u>beneficial</u> stress that motivates us). Coming from the same root as the word euphoria, eustress has been shown to induce ②<u>different</u> physiological changes to distress, including ③<u>more</u> strain on your cardiovascular system and a burst of the love hormone oxytocin, which helps ④<u>heal</u> damage to your heart.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ more → less. 유스트레스는 심혈관계에 '더 적은' 부담.
det.analysis:
❌ ① beneficial: 유익한. 적절.
❌ ② different: 다른. 적절.
✅ ③ more → less: 원문은 less strain. 반대.
❌ ④ heal: 치유하다. 적절.

questions.passage: When you are about to go on stage, do you feel sweaty, get ①<u>flushed</u>, have a dry mouth, or taste metal? These are signs of your body activating your stress ②<u>response</u> or sympathetic nervous system. But stress is bad, right? Actually, stress isn't always bad. There are two types of stress: distress and eustress (beneficial stress that ③<u>demotivates</u> us). Coming from the same root as the word euphoria, eustress has been shown to induce different ④<u>physiological</u> changes to distress.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ demotivates(동기 상실시키다) → motivates(동기 부여하다). 유스트레스는 '동기를 부여'함.
det.analysis:
❌ ① flushed: 달아오른. 적절.
❌ ② response: 반응. 적절.
✅ ③ demotivates → motivates: 원문 motivates. 반대.
❌ ④ physiological: 생리적. 적절.

det.analysis:

❌ ① avoidance: 회피. 문맥 부적절.
❌ ③ creation: 창조. 부적절.
❌ ④ prevention: 예방. 부적절.

questions.passage: But stress is bad, right? Actually, stress isn't always bad. det.analysis:

❌ ② discourages: 낙담시키다. 반대.
❌ ③ annoys: 짜증나게 하다. 부적절.
❌ ④ confuses: 혼란스럽게 하다. 부적절.
det.tip: motivate = 동기를 부여하다. 유사: encourage, inspire

❌ ③ eliminate: 제거하다. 부적절.
